mismatch.message: unsupported hero command: an unported branch of this command: quaffing requires djinni_from_bottle()

summary: The stop is caused by js/potion.js:dodrink() unconditionally rejecting every smoky-description potion at the djinni branch. C consumes the occupant-chance roll first; in this recording the roll is rn2(13)=3, so the djinni is not released and C falls through to dopotion(), which produces “You feel better.” The missing owner is dodrink()’s smoky-potion gate, not djinni_from_bottle(), whose C helper is already represented in JS for the magic-lamp path.

source.branch: After dodrink() selects a potion whose description is smoky, C checks that PM_DJINNI is not G_GONE and draws rn2(POTION_OCCUPANT_CHANCE(mvitals[PM_DJINNI].born)). It calls djinni_from_bottle() only when that draw is zero; a nonzero draw falls through to dopotion(). In this recording the C log shows rn2(13)=3 at potion.c:609, so Djinni is available with born 0 but the chance fails and the potion effect is processed normally.
callers: C cmd.c command table binds q to potion.c:dodrink().
JS cmd.js:runQuaffCommand() calls potion.js:dodrink(state) for the quaff command.
dependencies: potion.c:drink_ok() and dodrink() use getobj() to select a potion, then objdescr_is() checks the shuffled description; the djinni condition also reads mvitals[PM_DJINNI].mvflags and .born.

hack.h:POTION_OCCUPANT_CHANCE(n) is 13 + 2*n. The recorded rn2(13) call establishes born 0 and that the not-G_GONE condition passed; the result 3 is nonzero, so dodrink() skips djinni_from_bottle() and returns dopotion(otmp).

C potion.c:djinni_from_bottle() has return type void. On a successful occupant roll, dodrink() ignores that return, calls useup(otmp), and returns ECMD_TIME. The existing JS potion.js:djinni_from_bottle() returns its monster object for internal state flow, but its live dorub() caller ignores it; a quaff caller must likewise discard it and preserve C’s useup/ECMD_TIME contract.

For the recorded nonzero roll, C potion.c:dopotion() dispatches through peffects() to peffect_healing(), consumes the potion, and returns ECMD_TIME; the screen and RNG log show this branch rather than a released djinni.

evidence: The saved evaluation challenges/evaluations/20260926140428-v6.json reports 3/4 screens, 2267/2276 RNG calls, and 3/4 cursors matched. Its first stop is segment 0 step 3 on key d, where JS raises the unsupported quaffing/djinni_from_bottle() error.

The recording challenges/cases/v6/v6-add2-healer-drink-potion.session.json uses moves “ qd”; key q opens the potion prompt and d selects the item. At segment 0 step 3, C logs “rn2(13)=3 @ dodrink(potion.c:609)” followed by “d(4,4)=10 @ peffect_healing(potion.c:1122)” and displays “You feel better.” Thus the occupant roll was nonzero and the actual C path fell through to dopotion(), rather than calling djinni_from_bottle().

C nethack-c/upstream/src/potion.c:601-615 gives the owner branch: the smoky-potion case calls djinni_from_bottle(otmp), useup(otmp), and returns ECMD_TIME only when Djinni is not G_GONE and rn2(POTION_OCCUPANT_CHANCE(born)) is zero; otherwise dodrink() reaches return dopotion(otmp). The bound 13 is consistent with born 0 under nethack-c/upstream/include/hack.h:1409, where POTION_OCCUPANT_CHANCE(n) is 13 + 2*n.

C nethack-c/upstream/src/potion.c:2815-2868 defines djinni_from_bottle() as void. JS already has its shared implementation in js/potion.js:284-357, and js/apply.js calls it for the magic-lamp path. The first stop instead comes from js/potion.js:1365-1374, where dodrink() throws for any smoky description without checking G_GONE or consuming the occupant-chance RNG draw.
